Client's stated must-haves: interventional psych therapies (named as THE primary qualifier), cash pay, commercial insurance accepted. PRIMARY gate: interventional_psych_offered (weight 50, required_for_bullseye + required_for_contender + floor_tier Contender) — unconfirmed routes to Manual Review per the primary-qualifier rule; confirmed floors the record at Contender. SECOND must-have: cash_pay_visible (25, required_for_bullseye). commercial_insurance_accepted (15) is deliberately softened to verification_required (not a Bullseye must-have) because interventional practices routinely accept commercial insurance without listing payers — double-gating payment would contradict the client's 'too early to rule out models' guidance. MODALITY confirmations add depth toward Bullseye and align with the client's competitive note that TMS/Spravato/ECT/VNS presence HELPS (category awareness): tms_offered (15), spravato_or_esketamine_offered (15), ketamine_therapy_offered (12, reinforces cash_pay_visible — infusion therapy is predominantly patient-pay, the classic rarely-printed cash-pay proxy), depression_treatment_focus (8, client: 'depression is co-morbid'). NO negative or exclude_if_yes signals in this draft — the client explicitly declined hard disqualifiers and red flags ('we need to be open; this is a prescription device'). Max positive weight 140; the two must-haves alone give ~54 fit (Contender via floor); must-haves + insurance + two modalities clear the 80-point Bullseye line. All signals three-state (yes/no/not_found) with word-for-word textual anchoring; a yes without evidence_text + source_url is downgraded by the sourcing gate. | product_context added 2026-08-19, sourced verbatim-or-close from prolivrx.com (home, how-it-works, clinical-evidence, patients, about pages) — PENDING CLIENT APPROVAL before the first client-facing run; see CARTRIDGE_NOTES.md. Payment/coverage claims are deliberately absent (site states only 'Coverage varies').
contact_strategy: Ask for the physician-owner or lead psychiatrist first. At larger practices or clinics with an established TMS / interventional program, ask instead for the practice manager or clinical director who runs that program — the client notes larger groups are often manager-driven.
product_context: Proliv Rx is an FDA-approved, prescription-only wearable neuromodulation device for adults with Major Depressive Disorder who have not responded adequately to at least one antidepressant — the only at-home prescription brain neuromodulation therapy for this population. Patients self-treat at home (two 40-minute sessions daily, 8-16 weeks) under physician direction with app-based PHQ-9 tracking; the prescribing practice adds no equipment, no chair time, and no extra staff — the manufacturer handles device logistics and patient support. In its randomized sham-controlled trial, 62% achieved clinically substantial improvement at 8 weeks versus 32% on sham.

signals.prompt_instruction: Does the website show, word-for-word, that the practice itself offers interventional or device-based psychiatric treatment? Answer "yes" ONLY when one or more of these terms appears verbatim as a service THIS practice provides: "TMS", "transcranial magnetic stimulation", "rTMS", "deep TMS", "Spravato", "esketamine", "ketamine", "ECT", "electroconvulsive therapy", "VNS", "vagus nerve stimulation", "interventional psychiatry", or "neuromodulation". A referral-out statement, an educational or blog page about these treatments, or a provider bio mentioning training in them is NOT "yes". Answer "no" ONLY when the site explicitly states it does not offer these treatments or offers therapy/counseling only with medication management explicitly excluded. Otherwise answer "not_found". Quote the exact matched phrase in evidence_text and put the page URL it came from in source_url.

Does the website show, word-for-word, that the practice supports cash-pay / self-pay or patient-paid services? Answer "yes" ONLY when one or more of these terms appears verbatim in a services, pricing, billing, or patient-information context: "cash pay", "cash-pay", "self pay", "self-pay", "out of pocket", "out-of-pocket", "private pay", "membership", "concierge", "package pricing", "fee schedule", "financing", "CareCredit", or "payment plans". Answer "no" ONLY when the page explicitly states only insurance is accepted or that self-pay is not available. Otherwise answer "not_found". Do NOT infer from the mere presence of services; the term must appear word-for-word. Quote the exact matched phrase in evidence_text and put the page URL in source_url.

Does the website show, word-for-word, that the practice accepts commercial insurance? Answer "yes" ONLY when the site names commercial payers or in-network language verbatim, e.g. "we accept insurance", "in-network", "PPO", "Aetna", "Cigna", "Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "UnitedHealthcare", "Anthem", or "Optum", in a billing/insurance/patient-information context. Answer "no" ONLY when the site explicitly states it does not accept insurance or is out-of-network only / self-pay only. Otherwise answer "not_found". Quote the exact matched phrase in evidence_text and put the page URL in source_url.

Does the website show, word-for-word, that THIS practice offers TMS? Answer "yes" ONLY when one of these appears verbatim as an in-house service: "TMS", "transcranial magnetic stimulation", "rTMS", "deep TMS", "NeuroStar", "BrainsWay", or "MagVenture". A referral-out statement or educational mention is NOT "yes". Answer "no" ONLY when the site explicitly states TMS is not offered. Otherwise answer "not_found". Quote the exact matched phrase in evidence_text and put the page URL in source_url.

Does the website show, word-for-word, that THIS practice administers Spravato or esketamine? Answer "yes" ONLY when "Spravato" or "esketamine" appears verbatim as an in-office service (REMS-certified treatment center language also counts). A referral-out statement or educational mention is NOT "yes". Answer "no" ONLY when the site explicitly states it is not offered. Otherwise answer "not_found". Quote the exact matched phrase in evidence_text and put the page URL in source_url.

Does the website show, word-for-word, that THIS practice provides ketamine treatment? Answer "yes" ONLY when one of these appears verbatim as an in-house service: "ketamine", "ketamine infusion", "ketamine-assisted therapy", or "IV ketamine". A referral-out statement or educational mention is NOT "yes". Answer "no" ONLY when the site explicitly states it is not offered. Otherwise answer "not_found". Quote the exact matched phrase in evidence_text and put the page URL in source_url.

Does the website show, word-for-word, that the practice treats depression as a named clinical focus? Answer "yes" ONLY when one of these appears verbatim in a conditions-treated or services context: "depression", "major depressive disorder", "MDD", "treatment-resistant depression", "TRD", or "mood disorders". A blog post or educational article alone is NOT "yes". Answer "no" ONLY when the site explicitly excludes mood disorders from its scope. Otherwise answer "not_found". Quote the exact matched phrase in evidence_text and put the page URL in source_url.
